# PhysicsConstraintLimits <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Physics](Blitz3D-Physics)

</div>


```blitzbasic
PhysicsConstraintLimits:Void constraint:Int32, lower:Float32, upper:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `constraint` | In | Int32 | required | The constraint. |
| `lower` | In | Float32 | required | The lower limit. |
| `upper` | In | Float32 | required | The upper limit. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets how far a constraint may move. For a hinge the angle in degrees (from -180 to 180, 0 is the pose when it was made), for a slider the position in world units, for a distance constraint the smallest and the largest distance, for a cone constraint the half angle in degrees (the upper value). Point and fixed constraints have no limits.

## Differences

* The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
